pages.text: Each day after class, Julia and Toby sneak off to the wood.
pages.picture: after class: Julia and Toby tiptoeing through the wooden garden gate into the woods, glancing back toward the house, sneaking off

pages.text: "I bet floating is like feelings," said Julia. "When you get upset, things zoom up. So let's start there."
pages.picture: in the clearing: Julia explaining like a teacher, one finger raised; Toby sitting on the grass listening carefully

pages.text: "Toby, lift up that tin can." Toby looks at the can. He huffs. He puffs. Not a thing.
pages.picture: a tin can standing on the mossy stump; Toby staring at it, straining, cheeks puffed out; Julia watching; nothing moves

pages.text: Toby gets cross. And the can zooms up, up, up, and lands in a tree!
pages.picture: Toby cross, spikes up; the tin can shooting up and getting stuck high in the branches of the big oak; Julia gaping up at it

pages.text: "Now that stick," said Julia. Toby looks hard at the stick.
pages.picture: Toby staring hard at a stick on the ground, spikes flat; Julia pointing at the stick; the tin can still stuck high up in the big oak

pages.text: The stick shoots up and bonks Julia on the chin! "Ow! Toby!"
pages.picture: comic: a stick flying up and bonking Julia on the chin, Julia staggering back with a hand on her chin; Toby wincing

pages.text: Toby droops. "I am no good at this," he said.
pages.picture: Toby slumped on the grass, wings drooping, very sad; Julia kneeling beside him, patting his back

pages.text: Day after day, it is the same. Cans zoom off. Sticks smash. Not one thing floats the right way.
pages.picture: chaos in the clearing: tin cans and sticks flying every which way, one splashing into the pond; Julia ducking; Toby cross with his spikes up
